paragraphs: R' Mansya, grandson of R' Musya.
He is mentioned in Yoma 4b according to the reading Hyman attributes to Sheiltot, Va’etchanan.
He reports in the name of R' Mansya the Great. In Midrash Tehillim, R' Mansya says, ‘A counsel containing the word of the Lord will stand.’

notes.text: The supplied Yoma locator ר: would ordinarily mean 200b and is unresolved. The heading gives a grandson of Rabbi Musya; it does not identify him with Rabbi Mansya the Great.

The saved whole Davidson Yoma4b scalar has the parenthesized Musya, grandson of Masya, reporting Musya, with Rabbah after the parenthesis. This is a matching saying beside supplied ר:, conventionally200b, not proof that printed dalet became resh or that a historical deletion occurred. Hyman’s Mansya/grandson-of-Musya/Mansya-the-Great chain is retained separately. The SheiltotVaetchanan attribution was not newly inspected, and EinYaakov/SederHaDorot search leads are not full primary witnesses. Hyman’s MidrashTehillim quote is retained without adding a section or identity. Unverified Mansya/Musya title expansions remain R'.

Hyman’s printed page 894 reads Yoma 4b, beside ר: in the supplied transcription. The consulted Davidson text has Musya, grandson of Masya, and Ein Yaakov has Mansya, grandson of Mansya. Sheiltot 28, in Vayeshev, gives Mansya son of Mansya in the name of Mansya the Great. The Va’etchanan reading attributed by Hyman remains unverified. The consulted Midrash Tehillim 1:17 attributes the counsel saying to Rabbi Manshia.
